source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"A narrow therapeutic index, where small exposure changes can cause loss of effect or serious dose-related toxicity.","B":"A wide therapeutic index, where a broad exposure range separates therapeutic effects from important toxicity.","C":"Complete absence of a therapeutic range, meaning no dose can be adjusted using clinical or laboratory monitoring.","D":"Unpredictable absorption alone, meaning monitoring is needed because gastrointestinal uptake cannot be characterized."}}
source_row.rationale: NTI drugs have a narrow margin between concentrations associated with efficacy and those associated with toxicity or therapeutic failure, so small exposure changes can be clinically important.
source_row.source_detail: FDA CDER discussion of NTI drugs: small differences in dose or blood concentration may lead to serious therapeutic failures or adverse drug reactions. Current FDA CDER NTI standards page rechecked 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
source_row.stem: Why do narrow-therapeutic-index (NTI) drugs require especially careful dose and exposure control?
